explanation: A complete, bounded pick-and-place method for the runtime instruction. Fresh RGB-D reviews identify the bottle and rack table 1, fit visible cap, neck, body and support geometry, and derive a pad-centered neck grasp and inset landing position. It preserves tool orientation, measures a real retention lift, checks bounded transfer segments, lowers gently, releases, retreats for a new view, and evaluates the actual support relation and finite-interval stability. Historical checkpoints preserve geometry and acknowledged phases without pretending to be current measurements. Unknown or inconsistent registration falls back to independently measured, semantically corresponding cap center/axis geometry; circular yaw is explicitly unobserved. One open-grasp correction, two measured obstacle-height detours and one stability recheck are bounded recoveries. Observed obstruction, incomplete visibility and self-occlusion are separate review outcomes. The method stops with numerical evidence when identity, local action justification, sensing or budgets are insufficient; it does not claim certified collision clearance or official success.
interface: Execute the supplied Python main(api) with only the documented runtime v2 API, np, math and geo. It returns a JSON-compatible object containing completion_proposed, evidence and phase, plus reason on incomplete execution or limitations on completion. All physical actions use api.control, directly for gripper transitions and stationary observation intervals, or through bounded api.drive leases. Review fields are declared at every call with exact enums and constrained pixel arrays. Reviews request at most five named regions and three named points initially, one cap region for correspondence recovery, or one obstacle point for a detour. Failed measurements are checked before geometry use. NumPy values are converted at API/checkpoint boundaries. Initial partial samples, fitted episode geometry, semantic references, pending actions, measured retention and final observations are checkpointed. Restarts revalidate affected dependencies and never automatically reopen a bottle during transfer. The source uses no task files, hidden object state, force sensor, collision planner or evaluator.
jev_protocol: Each control request has exactly x,y,z,rx,ry,rz,gripper choice questions. The compiler explicitly binds each axis selector in state.processed_features.axes.<axis>.goal_relation. Jev selects positive for increase, negative for decrease and hold for within_tolerance; rotational signs are world rotation-vector signs, with xyzw tool quaternions. The gripper question selects the unchanged open/close/keep objective, not an inferred grasp state. Program features supply the phase, semantic reference and historical geometry frame; the host supplies trusted current robot state, pad/TCP conversion, numerical pose errors and goal relations. Targets, margins, fit residuals, attachment discrepancies and support gaps are calculated in Python, never delegated as arithmetic to Jev. Host residual magnitudes are L2-limited by the specified translation/rotation bounds and per-axis tolerance deadbands; no answer is corrected. Drive leases handle ordinary feedback and terminate on reached, stalled or exhaustion; direct controls accept bounded moved updates and stop on explicit stalls. Reached means robot pose/gripper delivery only. Independent RGB-D motion versus measured hand motion and whole-bottle visual evidence establish retention. Structured image reviews, not Jev text choices, supply object observations and explicit unknown outcomes. After release, a different view, measured support relation, acknowledged observation interval, measured stationarity and final semantic review support a completion proposal, never native success.
